faq.q: Which WCAG levels does it check?
faq.a: For each pair it shows the contrast ratio and pass/fail for AA normal text (4.5:1), AA large text (3:1), AAA normal (7:1), AAA large (4.5:1) and non-text UI components (3:1). Large text means 24px, or 18.66px bold. You can enter colours as HEX, RGB or HSL, swap foreground and background, and see a live preview with headings, body text and sample buttons.

faq.q: What is the APCA number shown below the ratio?
faq.a: It's an estimated APCA Lc value from the draft WCAG 3 method, shown as an approximation (not the exact reference algorithm). It models how the eye perceives light-on-dark versus dark-on-light and font size, which the WCAG 2 ratio doesn't, and gives guidance like 'body text is comfortable' or 'large headline only'. Treat both as guidance and test with real users.

faq.q: Does it help fix a failing combination?
faq.a: Yes. When a pair fails AA, the Suggestions section searches lightness variations of your text and of your background to find passing alternatives, each with its new ratio and a one-click Apply. It keeps the hue and only moves lightness, so the brand feel is preserved. It also simulates protanopia, deuteranopia, tritanopia and achromatopsia so you can see the pair under colour-blindness.

faq.q: Can I test many pairs and export the results?
faq.a: Yes. Batch Mode takes one 'foreground, background' pair per line (HEX/RGB/HSL) and tables the ratio and AA/AAA results for each. You can save pairs (stored in your browser under ccPairs), export a text report or a CSV, and your last colours are restored on return. Keyboard shortcuts: S swaps, D downloads the report.
